question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Sib-pair split experiment to test whether survival is heritable
ideas.description: Expand a clone, then split sister cells into parallel wells and treat each separately, varying the time between split and treatment from hours to weeks. If survivor frequency is correlated between sisters at short delays and decorrelates at long delays, that quantifies how long the surviving state is remembered and separates heritable priming from moment-to-moment randomness.

ideas.title: Expressed lineage barcodes plus paired profiling of untreated relatives
ideas.description: Transduce cells with heritable, transcribed barcodes, then sequence both a drug-treated arm and an untreated arm sampled before treatment so that the ancestors and cousins of future survivors can be identified retrospectively. Comparing the pre-treatment molecular profiles of clones that go on to survive versus those that die points directly at the primed state rather than at post-treatment adaptation.

ideas.title: Live imaging of signaling and cell-cycle reporters through drug addition
ideas.description: Image cells carrying kinase-activity and cell-cycle reporters (for example ERK, AKT, CDK2 sensors) continuously from before dosing until survivors are visible, then trace each survivor backwards through the movie. This reveals whether survival is predicted by baseline pathway activity, by a quiescent or slow-cycling phase at the moment of exposure, or by how fast signaling rebounds after inhibition.

ideas.title: Chromatin and transcription factor state of rare pre-primed cells, with causal follow-up
ideas.description: Apply single-cell ATAC-seq or joint RNA/ATAC profiling to untreated populations and to survivors, looking for a rare subpopulation whose regulatory landscape already resembles the resistant end state. Candidate transcription factors nominated this way can then be tested causally with CRISPR activation or inhibition to see whether raising or lowering their frequency shifts the fraction of cells that survive.

ideas.title: Pooled genetic screens layered onto the surviving fraction
ideas.description: Run CRISPR knockout, CRISPRi, or ORF overexpression screens in the presence of drug and score which perturbations change the number of survivors rather than bulk growth, including screens performed on survivors to find dependencies specific to that state. This distinguishes genes that set how often the surviving state arises from genes required to maintain it once entered, and nominates combination treatments that collapse the surviving fraction.
